text: Hume reported that when he looked inward he could never catch an impression of a simple, persisting 'self' -- only particular perceptions -- and concluded that the self is a bundle of perceptions.
explanation: True. Hume's bundle theory denies any impression of a self distinct from the sequence of perceptions; the sense of a unified persisting self is a fiction the imagination imposes on closely connected perceptions. He also confessed in the Treatise's appendix that he could not fully explain what unifies the bundle.
